article.title: North Korea’s Binance hack raises global financial security concerns
paras: Editor's note: this story was translated from the original VOA Korean article.

Cybersecurity experts tell VOA that the recent North Korean hack of Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange is particularly concerning because of the speed of both the attack, and how quickly the hackers moved the assets through financial networks.

Michael Barnhart, lead nation-state threat researcher at California-based cybersecurity company DTEX, told VOA that “one of the most significant aspects of the Binance incident was the speed at which the stolen funds were transferred."
"Rather than holding onto the cryptocurrency, the attackers moved it to Chinese money launderers within minutes," he said.

More than $6.3 billion worth of virtual assets were stolen from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, and “about $2.8 billion was frozen before it could be fully laundered or integrated into North Korean control,” Barnhart said. Some $3.5 billion of the stolen cryptocurrency remains in circulation, and efforts to trace and freeze the funds are continuing.

Nick Carlsen is a senior Investigator at TRM Labs who spent 12 years as an intelligence analyst at the FBI initiating major U.S. investigations into North Korea's illicit financial networks. He told VOA in a recent interview the speed and scale of the response to the hack “were unprecedented." He said stablecoin issuers and industry partners moved quickly to freeze substantial assets, but recovering the remaining funds will be difficult because laundering methods have become increasingly complex.

"The stolen funds appeared to have been divided into tens of thousands of transactions, many of them seemingly automated, making them harder to trace," Carlsen said, noting that he expects a substantial portion of the proceeds will ultimately reach the North Korean government, “although the final amount that can be recovered remains uncertain."

Large cryptocurrency exchanges face security challenges because of their size and global reach. Carlsen said exchanges “with thousands of employees have numerous potential entry points for hackers." He said companies handling large amounts of financial assets therefore need multiple layers of security, so that a single compromised account or system cannot expose their holdings.

Analysts also point to the financial objectives behind North Korea’s cyber operations. While Russia and China have often focused on espionage, including the theft of sensitive information and industrial technology, North Korea has increasingly used cyber operations to generate revenue.

“Cybercrime and cryptocurrency theft have become the North Korean government’s largest single source of foreign currency," he said. "The proceeds can be used for a range of government activities, including potentially supporting the country’s nuclear and missile programs."
Barnhart said North Korea has little reason to stop targeting cryptocurrency exchanges.

Previous attacks on platforms including Axie Infinity and Bybit, followed by the Binance breach, show that the sector remains an attractive target. The financial returns remain substantial, while the risks to the North Korean government are comparatively limited.
Both experts said stronger corporate cybersecurity measures are necessary but insufficient to address the threat.
Barnhart argued that “companies can do only so much to defend themselves against repeated attacks without a policy response."
"Governments, particularly the United States and South Korea, must take a more active role in responding to North Korea’s cyber theft operations," added Carlsen.

The Binance breach is part of a series of major cryptocurrency thefts attributed to North Korea. While exchanges continue to strengthen their defenses, the experts say a broader response from governments will be needed to disrupt the networks that move and launder stolen funds.
zh: 北韓對幣安的駭客攻擊引發全球對金融安全的擔憂
編者註：本文翻譯自美國之音（VOA）的韓文原文報導。
網路安全專家向美國之音表示，北韓近期對全球最大加密貨幣交易所幣安（Binance）發動的駭客攻擊之所以特別令人擔憂，在於攻擊速度之快，以及駭客將資產透過金融網路轉移的速度之快。
總部位於加州的網路安全公司 DTEX 的首席國家級威脅研究員麥可·巴恩哈特（Michael Barnhart）向美國之音表示：「幣安事件中最值得注意的方面之一，就是被盜資金轉移的速度之快。」
「攻擊者並未持有這些加密貨幣，而是在幾分鐘內便將其轉移給中國的洗錢者，」他表示。
全球最大的加密貨幣交易所幣安（Binance）遭竊的虛擬資產價值超過 63 億美元，巴恩哈特表示：「其中約 28 億美元在完全洗錢或被納入北韓控制之前已被凍結。」 其中約35億美元的遭竊加密貨幣仍處於流通狀態，當局正持續進行追蹤與凍結相關資金的行動。
尼克·卡爾森（Nick Carlsen）是 TRM Labs 的資深調查員，他曾在聯邦調查局（FBI）擔任情報分析師長達 12 年，負責啟動針對北韓非法金融網絡的重大美國調查。他在最近接受美國之音（VOA）採訪時表示，此次對駭客攻擊的應對速度與規模「前所未有」。 他表示，穩定幣發行方和業界合作夥伴已迅速採取行動凍結了大量資產，但由於洗錢手法日益複雜，要追回剩餘資金將十分困難。
卡爾森表示：「被盜資金似乎已被拆分成數萬筆交易，其中許多交易看似是自動進行的，這使得追蹤更加困難。」他同時指出，預計這筆贓款中相當大一部分最終將流入北韓政府手中，「儘管最終能追回的金額仍不確定。」
大型加密貨幣交易所因其規模龐大且業務遍及全球，因而面臨安全挑戰。卡爾森表示，擁有數千名員工的交易所「存在眾多潛在的駭客入侵點」。他指出，因此，處理大量金融資產的公司需要多層次的安全防護，以確保即使單一帳戶或系統遭入侵，也不會導致其持有的資產外洩。
分析師們也指出，北韓網路行動背後存在著財務目的。雖然俄羅斯和中國往往著重於間諜活動——包括竊取敏感資訊和工業技術——但北韓卻越來越多地利用網路行動來創造收入。
「網路犯罪和加密貨幣竊盜已成為北韓政府最大的單一外匯來源，」他表示。「這些所得可用於各項政府活動，包括可能用於支持該國的核武與飛彈計畫。」
巴恩哈特表示，北韓幾乎沒有理由停止將加密貨幣交易所作為攻擊目標。
先前針對 Axie Infinity 和 Bybit 等平台的攻擊事件，以及隨後的幣安（Binance）資料外洩事件，均顯示該領域仍是極具吸引力的攻擊目標。此類攻擊能帶來可觀的財務回報，而對北韓政府而言，相關風險相對有限。
兩位專家均表示，雖然企業必須加強網路安全措施，但僅靠這些措施並不足以應對這項威脅。
巴恩哈特指出：「若缺乏政策層面的因應措施，企業在面對反覆發動的攻擊時，能採取的自衛措施終究有限。」
卡爾森補充道：「各國政府，尤其是美國和南韓，必須在應對北韓的網路竊取行動方面發揮更積極的作用。」
幣安（Binance）遭駭事件是被歸咎於北韓的一系列重大加密貨幣盜竊案之一。儘管各交易所持續加強防禦措施，但專家表示，若要瓦解那些用於轉移及洗錢的網絡，仍需各國政府採取更廣泛的應對措施。
